content.body: keithamus: I think I found a way out of the `customelementregistry` attribute mess. Since the main point of conflict is the reflected attribute, we'll give that a somewhat unusual name: `htmlCustomElementRegistry`.
content.formatted_body: keithamus: I think I found a way out of the customelementregistry attribute mess. Since the main point of conflict is the reflected attribute, we'll give that a somewhat unusual name: htmlCustomElementRegistry.

content.body: As you would hardly ever use that it seems like a fine solution for this problem.

dandclark  I just checked https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995 while trying to address review comments for Firefox's patches and IIUC:
- Delan's comments can be resolved now (I don't have the permission to do that): https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#discussion_r4151720877 https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#discussion_r4151721059 https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#discussion_r4182302141 https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#discussion_r4182390405 https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#discussion_r4182412125
- Regarding smaug 's comments about submitter/source, I understand you are saying it's less risky for webcompat to use a retargeted internal value set at init time (not based on relatedTarget). submitter does not do retargeting though, so this is blocker, but you are ok to take the same approach as for source.
- Another blocker is from annevk 's AI feedback is about the unconditionally set composed flag, which would be addressed by aligning the spec on what Chromium implements.
